No predecessor PR is attributed. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 5 items remain** Keep open. The missing-callback fallback addresses a real silent-terminal path, but it newly permits durable transcript writes from detached runs and can leave a committed fallback after cancellation while returning the original cancelled attempt. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `3590b70f21aeb8f5483e4cd451fb5bd24e614b01` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | The branch has a focused, net-negative approach, but two concrete session-state defects and mock-only behavior evidence block merge readiness. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | Needs real behavior proof before merge: The supplied evidence is a fixture-driven direct call to the terminal-finalization owner with a mocked harness callback; it does not provide an after-fix run through a real missing-callback harness and delivery boundary. If it does not, the PR author or someone with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 7 items | Introduced trigger: The PR removes the availability gate, so an otherwise eligible turn with no callback now proceeds into finalization; the generic harness selector then throws for a missing callback, which reaches the fallback branch.
Detached-session contract: The run parameter contract states that detached runs never write durable transcript or metadata, but the newly reachable fallback unconditionally invokes transcript persistence and its helper has no detached-session guard.
Cancellation persistence race: The transcript writer can append before its next abort check; an abort then throws, the fallback helper catches and suppresses it, and the outer branch returns the original attempt after observing cancellation. The durable append is therefore not represented by the returned terminal state. | | **Findings** | 2 actionable findings | [P2] Preserve detached transcript isolation
[P2] Reconcile a committed fallback with cancellation | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together Embedded agent runs execute tools through a selected harness and then resolve a terminal reply for the session. This change affects the fallback path used after settled tools when no harness finalizer can produce a visible answer. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Settled tool turn] --> B[Terminal resolution] B --> C{Finalizer callback available?} C -->|yes| D[Harness finalization] C -->|no| E[Host fallback] D --> F[Session delivery] E --> G[Transcript mirror] G --> F ``` ## Before merge - [ ] **Add real behavior proof** - Needs real behavior proof before merge: The supplied evidence is a fixture-driven direct call to the terminal-finalization owner with a mocked harness callback; it does not provide an after-fix run through a real missing-callback harness and delivery boundary. Add a redacted terminal trace or runtime log showing one fallback without replay, plus the detached and cancellation outcomes; updating the PR body should trigger a fresh ClawSweeper review, or a maintainer can request `@clawsweeper re-review`. After adding proof, update the PR body; ClawSweeper should re-review automatically. If it does not, the PR author or someone with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. - [ ] **Preserve detached transcript isolation (P2)** - The removed availability gate newly sends callback-less detached runs into `persistSettledToolFallbackTranscript()`. That helper writes through the resolved durable session target even though detached runs must never write transcript state; skip the mirror append for `sessionPersistence: "detached"` and cover the absent-callback case. - [ ] **Reconcile a committed fallback with cancellation (P2)** - A callback-less turn can append its fallback, then observe cancellation in the transcript writer or outer post-append check and return the original cancelled attempt. The durable transcript now contains a fallback that the terminal result denies; make the write cancellation-atomic or retain the committed fallback outcome, and test an append that commits before cancellation. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P2)** - Merging as written can leak a detached helper run’s synthesized fallback into a durable conversation transcript and can retain a fallback after cancellation despite reporting the original cancelled result. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)** - Repair detached and cancellation fallback persistence, add the two boundary regressions, and provide redacted real behavior proof before merge. ## Findings - [P2] Preserve detached transcript isolation — `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/settled-turn-finalization.ts:205-210` - [P2] Reconcile a committed fallback with cancellation — `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/settled-turn-finalization.ts:211-221`

Yes, from source: remove the callback on a detached eligible settled turn or cancel immediately after the transcript append commits; both newly reach the inconsistent fallback persistence path. Confidence: 0.98 - [P2] Reconcile a committed fallback with cancellation — `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/settled-turn-finalization.ts:211-221` A callback-less turn can append its fallback, then observe cancellation in the transcript writer or outer post-append check and return the original cancelled attempt. The durable transcript now contains a fallback that the terminal result denies; make the write cancellation-atomic or retain the committed fallback outcome, and test an append that commits before cancellation. What I checked: - **Introduced trigger:** The PR removes the availability gate, so an otherwise eligible turn with no callback now proceeds into finalization; the generic harness selector then throws for a missing callback, which reaches the fallback branch. ([`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/terminal-resolution.ts:120`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3590b70f21aeb8f5483e4cd451fb5bd24e614b01/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/terminal-resolution.ts#L120), [3590b70f21ae](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3590b70f21aeb8f5483e4cd451fb5bd24e614b01)) - **Detached-session contract:** The run parameter contract states that detached runs never write durable transcript or metadata, but the newly reachable fallback unconditionally invokes transcript persistence and its helper has no detached-session guard. Runtime, network, CSP, and security claims still need visible diagnostics. ### Workflow - ClawSweeper keeps one durable marker-backed review comment per issue or PR. - Re-runs edit this comment so the latest verdict, findings, and automation markers stay together instead of adding duplicate bot comments. - A fresh review can be triggered by eligible `@clawsweeper re-review` comments, exact-item GitHub events, scheduled/background review runs, or manual workflow dispatch. - PR/issue authors and users with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review` or `@clawsweeper re-run` on an open PR or issue to request a fresh review only. - Maintainers can also comment `@clawsweeper review` to request a fresh review only. - Fresh-review commands do not start repair, autofix, rebase, CI repair, or automerge. - Maintainer-only repair and merge flows require explicit commands such as `@clawsweeper autofix`, `@clawsweeper automerge`, `@clawsweeper fix ci`, or `@clawsweeper address review`. - Maintainers can comment `@clawsweeper explain` to ask for more context, or `@clawsweeper stop` to stop active automation.
